title: A Network Analysis of Teachers’ Coping With Preschoolers’ Negative Emotions
abstract: Teachers’ coping with children’s negative emotions (TCCNE) plays a key role in shaping preschoolers’ social skills and socio-emotional development during early childhood. This study used network analysis to examine the interrelationships among six coping reaction orientations: distress reactions (DR), punitive reactions (PR), minimization reactions (MR), expressive encouragement (EE), emotion-focused reactions (EFR), and problem-focused reactions (PFR). Participants included 241 preschool teachers (240 women; M age = 32.63 years, SD = 7.94). Teachers completed the Coping with Children’s Negative Emotions Scale, which comprises six dimensions. Findings revealed that emotion-focused and problem-focused coping orientations were most central in the network, linked to each other and to EE. DR and PR were also closely connected. These patterns were broadly similar across the career stages examined. These findings deepen our understanding of how preschool teachers’ coping orientations are structured and interconnected.

journal.name: JOURNAL OF EMOTIONAL AND BEHAVIORAL DISORDERS
